# Panel J2: first-time visitor, round 1

I judged only from the reader contact sheets: 13 at 1440 and 12 at 1024, with `clips-panel.json` for the screen map and `scenes/1440` for static context. Full data is in `panel-j2.json`.

## Scores

| Keep scrolling | Tempo | Discovery |
|---|---|---|
| 3 / 5 | 3 / 5 | 2 / 5 |

I would keep scrolling on 31 of 49 screens at 1440 (63 %) and 34 of 53 at 1024 (64 %).

## Acts

| Act | 1440 yes | 1024 yes | Tempo | Feel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opening: play, broom flight, name | 1/1 | 1/1 | medium | A real hook. The empty-sea hold and ~16 s before you can scroll make it a touch long. |
| I · The Crossing (Pirates) | 6/7 (86 %) | 6/7 (86 %) | medium | The porthole reveal and chapter list flow well. The About text wall slows it, and the third sea photo drags. |
| II · The Workshop (3 Idiots) | 9/15 (60 %) | 11/18 (61 %) | slow | Starts great (wave wipe, zoom-through, chalkboard), then two projects in one identical template, a skills table and a long kill-list. |
| Interlude · Three films and a game | 5/7 (71 %) | 5/6 (83 %) | brisk | After a dead title screen, a new palette on every screen, a quill and typed titles, and the snitch. The most fun stretch. |
| III · The Frontier (Red Dead) | 6/11 (55 %) | 7/13 (54 %) | medium | Grand opening, then a sag in the middle: the same dawn photo four times and essay stubs marked "soon". The WANTED poster and testimonials recover it. |
| IV · The Light (Harry Potter) | 4/6 (67 %) | 4/6 (67 %) | medium | The burn transition and Great Hall are magic. Five identical principle boxes crawl and look choppy. |
| Credits | 0/2 | 0/2 | slow | Tiny grey type on black. This is where I'd leave. |

## What invited me to play

- **Most inviting:** the golden snitch (1440 screen 29, 1024 screen 32). I want to chase it, but it is tiny and fast.
- **Other things I'd try:** the Play button (screen 1), the spyglass bracket around the Black Pearl (screen 1), Jack's compass (screen 4), the backtest chart toggles (1440 screen 18, 1024 screen 20), the satchel items (1440 screen 36, 1024 screen 39) and the email pill.
- **The promised game:** "Three films and a game" made me look for one. In the capture I never found anything that plainly said *play me*. The Dead Eye squares appear only at 1024 (screen 30) and read as debris.

## Top problems

1. **High.** A "HARRY POTTER" heading sits over the Red Dead campfire photo, still captioned as Red Dead, for 2–4 s. This is at 1440 screen 41 (#104) and at 1024 screen 45 (#98).
2. The second project repeats the first project's template and the same corridor photo (1440 screens 16–17, #46–50).
3. "Three films and a game" is a near-empty black screen for ~4 s (1440 screen 24, #67).
4. Image seams leave dark gaps: the lecture hall into the pen (1440 screen 10, #33) and the dawn into the dawn again (1440 screen 32, #83).
5. An empty outlined box sits in the kill-list row and looks like a broken image (1440 screen 22, #61).
6. A thick grey brush-arc artifact appears in the journal (1440 screen 39, #99; 1024 screen 43, #93).
7. At 1024 the cloud wipe pauses on a blank texture with a ring, which reads as loading (screen 10, #27).
8. Several blocks are walls of small, low-contrast text: About (1440 #19), the kill-list (#64), the testimonials (#103) and the credits (#122).
9. Headings and photos repeat. The Red Dead and Harry Potter headings each appear twice, the Black Pearl and pen photos are reused, and the dawn photo appears four times.
10. The principles are five identical boxes, and the capture log shows ~5 fps there (1440 #114–117).
